chosen.content:
Review: The assumption that Layer 1 must be exactly the top-view footprint  
\(F=\{(1,1),(1,2),(1,3),(2,1)\}\) is correct. Any top-view 1 needs bottom support somewhere below it, so Layer 1 must include those cells; any Layer-1 block outside \(F\) would make an observed 0 become 1 in the top view.

Failed decision/evidence: The attempt fixing Layer 2 to exactly \((1,1)\) and \((2,1)\), then leaving Layer 3 undecided, produced a valid but repeated candidate with reward \(-1\) (outcome with Layer 2 rows “1 0 0 / 1 0 0” and no Layer 3). This shows that continuing to hand-pick small Layer-2 masks is not productive.

Repeated structural direction: Most attempts keep Layer 2 equal or nearly equal to \(F\), or force most/all footprint columns to height \(\ge 2\), then refine Layer-3 masks. This over-samples tall-column profiles.

Suggested different operation: Switch from mask refinement to systematic height-tuple exploration over the four fixed columns, prioritizing lower/minimal profiles and omission/minimization checks rather than further subdividing Layer-3 masks.

Next actionable adjustment: Generate an untried height tuple with fewer tall columns, and explicitly check whether reducing/removing upper-layer entries still preserves the required top-view footprint.

Constraint to check: For every candidate, verify contiguous support from Layer 1, no block outside \(F\) in any upper layer, no unnecessary empty top layer, and novelty against the previously observed height tuples.

rejected.content:
Review: The prior attempts fix Layer 1 to exactly the four top-view occupied cells, but this assumes Layer 1 must fully cover the top-view footprint, which is not required. The top view is the union of all layers, so Layer 1 could be a subset of those cells, with other layers covering the remaining positions.  
Constraint check: The bottom layer (Layer 1) must contain at least one block, but it is not required to match the full top-view footprint. Fixing Layer 1 to exactly four cells unnecessarily restricts valid configurations.  
Next direction: Explore Layer 1 with fewer blocks (e.g., only (1,1), (1,2), (1,3)) and let Layer 2 or 3 cover the (2,1) position, ensuring support constraints and the top view is fully covered.
